items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: I was wondering if Omer Simeon wasn't a more important influence on the younger white Chicago players

ctx.x: He tried, but he played too easily for that. He had too much serenity about his playing. The younger white Chicago guys had something else in mind. They admired Noon's technique, and they learned all they could from it, and the bending of the notes and everything, but... Noon's influence stopped at the point of hot playing, and we were talking earlier, John, about Omer Simeon, and I was wondering if Omer Simeon wasn't a more important influence on the younger white Chicago players. I don't know.
You see a closer relationship, do you, between Simeon and the white style than between any of the other...
